script.label: Problem
script.text: An agent that can place orders will sooner or later send a bad one: too big, based on a stale price, or in the wrong unit. Anyone building an agent on Solana needs a plain check between the idea and the action. Without it, one wrong number moves real money.

script.label: What it does
script.text: This is a small agent. It reads recorded Orca SOL/USDC swaps, cuts them into 20,000 dollar bars, wakes on an 8 basis point change alert and proposes one order per alert. A risk hook checks each order against the Pyth oracle and answers yes or no, with the rule that decided. Accepted orders go into a ledger.

script.label: Live proof
script.text: Here it runs on 1,114 real swaps: 10 change alerts, 9 orders accepted, 1 refused (1 by max-notional). Now the failure test: I feed it 4 bad orders, a 5,000 dollar order, a 300 second old oracle, a price in cents and a price 100 basis points off. All 4 are refused, each with its reason. Reads are public mainnet data; writes are devnet only. On devnet, the node verifies my signed memo transaction, but the faucet was rate limited, so there is no funded transaction link yet.

script.label: Limit and next
script.text: Limits: this is simulated on recorded data, about seventeen minutes of one afternoon. The order sizes and the fee are assumptions, and no order was sent anywhere. The ledger is not evidence of returns. Next: write one funded devnet memo for every accepted order, and run the same hook on the live feed.

checks.text: No part ran more than 10 s over its budget
Said who has the problem in the first 30 seconds
Showed one live action, not only a slide
Ran the failure test and showed the refusal
Opened a devnet link, or said there is none and why
Made no return or profit claim
A listener can restate the claim in one sentence
